newsitem.title: ITALY: Bertinotti rules pensioners out of Italy budget.
newsitem.headline: Bertinotti rules pensioners out of Italy budget.

text.p: The leader of Italy's hard-line Communist Refoundation party said on Wednesday that it would refuse to discuss a forthcoming mini-budget with the government if it tried to raise cash from pensioners.
Fausto Bertinotti told Italian state television RAI that if the measures called for a soldiarity contribution from pensioners "talks with the government won't even start."

A senior member of the Democratic Party of the Left, the biggest in Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government, had floated the idea of a "solidarity contribution" from those who took early retirement on the same RAI news programme.
Fabio Mussi, PDS leader in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) told RAI that such a contribution was "one of the things that could be studied...We have to work out how together."

Prodi, who relies on support from Communist Refoundation for a parliamentary majority, announced earlier that the government would pass a mini-budget in the next few weeks to ensure it was ready for a European single currency due to start in 1999.
Bertinotti said earlier he would be ready to discuss the package provided it did not contain spending cuts or new taxes.

Gianfranco Fini, leader of the hard-right National Alliance party, said that the fact the government had now decided to pass a mini-budget proved that its 1997 austerity package, designed to slash 62.5 trillion lire ($37 billion) off this year's deficit, had not done enough to tame unruly state finances.
"If the (mini-budget) is done with new taxes, even levied on pensioners, the government can forget about help from the Freedom Alliance," Fini said, referring to the centre-right opposition bloc.
